### Add an allow list for false-positive findings: an agent proposes a finding by id, a person approves it at a terminal, and check stops raising that value without a rescan

[`8581de750671`](https://github.com/pilifs/in-the-loop/commit/8581de750671ab8b5a7027cd74d3e0c85e2549f4) · [log `25e4c41e4dcb`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/20803daf-7ba0-4214-a79c-415a27f48a7b/25e4c41e4dcb79e336fcd0b1da3d8e468a4f8559738bea84b4407af0e0b76b45.jsonl.gz)

Work from session 0d3dce51, committed from another session at the user's request so that the repository could be pushed; its description here is read from the diff. Accepting a finding by id meant finding the value again with a scan of every file newer than the redaction stamp, and a class of false positives (version numbers that look like addresses) used to be settled by a new rule, which voided the stamp and rescanned everything. llm-dlc/allowlist.json settles them by value instead, through a new 'allow' command: listing entries with proposals masked, 'propose ID --reason' recording a proposal with the id, kind and masked value (open to agents), an approval step that prints the real values and asks a person once for 'false positive', direct entry of a value by a person, and 'drop' to remove entries. The list is published with its values, so it takes only the kinds the redactor leaves in a log and that are published anyway once accepted (public-ip, ipv6, mac-address, other-home-dir, auth-header, long-token); a finding the redactor would remove still goes through review accept, which keeps only a hash. The project settings deny agents the approval and direct-entry steps and direct edits to the list; CLAUDE.md, llm-dlc/README.md, the specification and the review-findings skill describe the new procedure, and the list of reviewed findings carries the entries a person recorded meanwhile. Verified: llm-dlc/tools/test_review.py, 25 tests, passes.

### Feature loop: keep a record of each run with the session's closing summary, let the session decide when to stop by instructions given on the command line or in a brief, and work from markdown briefs, starting with one to make sync.py fast

[`797a84d5a358`](https://github.com/pilifs/in-the-loop/commit/797a84d5a358a9154110b68ddadb81554852de64) · [log `7c0df4e6d7ba`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/20803daf-7ba0-4214-a79c-415a27f48a7b/7c0df4e6d7baac5a82353f223d347b0413c25e9308853e2529ccaa90f81a8732.jsonl.gz)

Record: each run of llm-dlc/tools/feature-loop.sh writes llm-dlc/loop-summaries/DATE-PROMPT.md (gitignored, never pushed) with the instruction, a line per commit as it lands so that it survives a restart, and how the run ended. When it ends normally the session gets one more turn that only reports, a Markdown summary of the run's commits, pending or failed verification jobs, sync.py check warnings to judge before pushing and work deferred for the user's input, which the loop takes from the turn's result event and appends.

Stopping: feature-loop.sh PROMPT [CYCLES] [UNTIL]. With UNTIL (a second argument that is not a count counts as UNTIL), each commit is followed, before the compact, by a turn in which the session weighs UNTIL against the run's commits and ends with 'LOOP: continue' or 'LOOP: stop'; stop ends the run with its summary, a reply with neither stops it as needing attention (exit 1), and a count stays an upper limit. Decisions and their reasons go into the record.

Briefs: PROMPT may be a markdown file. Each cycle tells the session to read it again in full and take the next piece of work it calls for that the run's commits have not done, so it outlives every compact; its hash is recorded and a brief that changes during the run stops the loop. A brief's '## Loop until' section is its default UNTIL. FEATURE_LOOP_SESSION=ID resumes another session and FEATURE_LOOP_SESSION=new starts a fresh one for the run. The first brief, llm-dlc/loops/sync-performance.md, is an outside review of sync.py's performance (full syncs on every commit, a check that decompresses about 2.75 GB of history, a quadratic email regex, granular jj queries, synchronous Langfuse export, serial uploads) turned into a plan, with rules for the loop: measure every change, weaken no redaction or publication guarantee, keep published bytes identical, push nothing, and defer explicitly whatever needs the user (credentials, external services, decisions) in a 'Deferred for the user' paragraph; it runs until most of the reasonably attainable value is realized.

Verified with stubbed claude and jj inside the real systemd scope: fixed counts, an empty summary, a cycle with no commit, continue/continue/stop decisions, an unclear decision, a count with UNTIL, argument errors, a brief from another directory with a fresh session, the brief's Loop until section as default and a command-line UNTIL overriding it, a brief edited mid-run and a missing brief. llm-dlc/README.md documents all of it.

### langfuse-loop.sh: send unsent turns to Langfuse as they appear

[`a28b1f4686a3`](https://github.com/pilifs/in-the-loop/commit/a28b1f4686a3f75e300180bf22b3598e7d6877e7) · [log `7651620c8fd1`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/20803daf-7ba0-4214-a79c-415a27f48a7b/7651620c8fd147305a7a1be099e0c4ba0843076dfeb154970ae5cbc793e510d2.jsonl.gz)

sync.py langfuse gains --pending (sessions whose latest stored log has turns not yet sent; a state-file mark by log sha keeps the check cheap) and --all (send them). llm-dlc/tools/langfuse-loop.sh polls that list, runs --all, retries while Langfuse is down, and takes stop/now/? commands like verification-loop.sh, with no Claude session. Verified against the local Langfuse: 19 pending sessions sent, then the loop idles on 'nothing to send'.

> Update the feature loop to give the agent executing the feature the ability to arbitrarily signal when a feature is completing, rather than running for a fixed number of iterations. If this option is selected, it should be a second (optional) input into feature-loop which are instructions the agent should consider upon iteration completion to determine whether to start a new loop or end the loop with that iteration post-commit.

**Reply:**

The feature loop now takes an optional instruction for when the work is done, and the agent decides when to stop. Tests with a stubbed agent pass. It's still not committed, together with the run-record change: the other session's allow-list work is still uncommitted in the same working copy, and `llm-dlc/README.md` has edits from both of us.

**Usage:** `feature-loop.sh PROMPT [CYCLES] [UNTIL]`. A second argument that isn't a number is read as UNTIL, so both of these work:
```bash
llm-dlc/tools/feature-loop.sh spring "Stop once the throws lines cover reactive handlers, or when the next idea would be minor."
llm-dlc/tools/feature-loop.sh spring 8 "…"   # the session decides, with 8 cycles as a cap
```

**How it decides:**
- After each commit, and before the compact, the session gets one more turn while it still has the cycle in context.
- That turn passes it your UNTIL text and the run's commits (`jj log -r START..@-`). It answers with a short reason and a last line of `LOOP: continue` or `LOOP: stop`. The parsing tolerates backticks and bold around that line.
- **Continue:** the loop compacts and runs the next cycle.
- **Stop:** the loop compacts, writes the run summary and exits 0, the same as running out of cycles.
